title: TritonGym: A Benchmark for Agentic LLM Workflows in Triton GPU Code Generation
claim: A unified benchmark bundles datasets, standard tools and an evaluation pipeline around an agentic workflow, so agent designs can be compared fairly.
layout: Top agent-workflow strip over three boxed modules, bidirectional arrows between them
description: A wide, two-tier diagram. The top green band shows an Agentic Workflow with an OpenAI-style logo: four boxes in a row (Task Planning, Code Generation, Evaluator, Performance Summarization) joined by arrows, with a feedback loop returning to Task Planning. A large arrow leads to a pink box labeled Triton Kernel containing a short code snippet. Below, a light-blue region labeled TritonGym Benchmark holds three rounded panels. Dataset has six icon-labeled blue tiles (Operator Definition, DSL Description, Oracle Example, Hardware Specification, Input Specification, Tool Documentation). Standard Tools has Profiler, Compiler, Browser, Verifier, Searcher and Evaluator. Evaluation Pipeline has Verifier and Evaluator, with small correctness and performance icons. Gray arrows labeled Task Description, Function Calls, Tool Feedbacks and Output Kernel connect the tiers. The eye lands first on the green workflow strip, then moves down to the blue modules.
caption: An overview of TritonGym.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can already draft plausible Triton kernels, yet most existing evaluations still focus on single-shot generation and underplay tool use and feedback. We introduce TritonGym , a benchmark and orchestration framework for evaluating agentic workflows in GPU code generation. TritonGym standardizes access to a set of code generation tools via function-calls, separating intrinsic model capability from workflow design and enabling fair, apples-to-apples comparison. The benchmark spans a maintained operator set, community samples, out-of-distribution tasks, and DSL extensions, ensuring both generality and extensibility. By providing a common orchestration and evaluation framework, TritonGym democratizes the development of GPU coding agents, supports practical adoption of agent-generated kernels, and facilitates progress on advanced agentic systems.
